actor.why: French loan in -eur takes -s: de acteur -> de acteurs; 'Acteuren' is the script's default -en rule

alligator.why: de alligator -> de alligators. The -or -> -oren plural is restricted to Latin agent nouns (motor, professor, tractor); alligator is an animal name with initial stress and takes -s

ambulance.why: French loan ending in schwa: de ambulance -> de ambulances; 'Ambulancen' is not Dutch

angel.why: de engel -> de engelen (irregular -en on a stem in -el). 'Engels' is not a plural at all; it reads as the language/adjective 'Engels' (English) and would be spoken that way by TTS

armchair.why: French loan: de fauteuil -> de fauteuils; 'Fauteuilen' is the script's default -en rule

artist.why: de kunstenaar -> de kunstenaars is the standard dictionary plural for this -aar agent noun; 'Kunstenaren' is at best marginal and unsuitable for K-3 TTS

asparagus.why: de asperge -> de asperges (stem ends in schwa -> -s). 'Aspergen' is not Dutch. N1 is a false suspicion: asperge is countable in Dutch (twee asperges)

author.why: French loan in -eur takes -s: de auteur -> de auteurs

baby-overall.why: English loan: de overall -> de overalls; 'Baby-overallen' is the script's default -en rule

badge.why: English loan: de badge -> de badges; 'Badgen' is not Dutch and would be read as a verb

barbecue.why: English loan: de barbecue -> de barbecues; 'Barbecuen' would be read as a verb

bee.why: de bij -> de bijen. 'Bijjen' is an impossible Dutch spelling: <ij> is a digraph and is never doubled by the consonant-doubling rule the script applied

bison.why: de bizon -> de bizons. Stress is on the first syllable, so the script's consonant doubling ('Bizonnen') does not apply

blouse.why: de blouse -> de blouses; French loan in -e takes -s, not the script's -en

blue-jay.why: de gaai -> de gaaien; the apostrophe-s is wrong (only after a/i/o/u/y-final words) and the adjective already ends in -e so it does not change

broccoli.why: mass/vegetable noun: de broccoli has no child-level plural; 'Broccoli's' is script output. p must equal s ('Broccoli')

brownie.why: de brownie -> de brownies; English loan takes -s. 'Brownien' is not Dutch

butter.why: mass noun: de boter has no child-level plural; 'Boters' is script output. p must equal s ('Boter')

cabana.why: de cabine -> de cabines; loan in unstressed -e takes -s, not -n

calculator.why: de rekenmachine -> de rekenmachines; noun in unstressed -e takes -s. 'Rekenmachinen' is script output

calf.why: het kalf -> de kalveren (irregular -eren plural); 'Kalven' comes from a -lf->-lven rule that does not apply here

canary.why: de kanarie -> de kanaries; nouns in unstressed -ie take -s. 'Kanarien' is script output

cape.why: de cape -> de capes; loan in -e takes -s. 'Capen' is not Dutch

cashier.why: 'Kassieren' is script output and is wrong under any reading: nouns in -ier take -s (bankier -> bankiers, kassier -> kassiers). If the singular HOLD swaps the lemma, the plural follows that lemma instead

cast.why: het gips is a mass noun (the material/the cast on an arm); no child-level plural. p must equal s ('Gips'). 'het gipsverband' would be the countable alternative, but that is a different lemma

celery.why: de selderij is a mass/vegetable noun with no child-level plural; 'Selderijjen' is a script consonant-doubling artefact and is not Dutch. p must equal s ('Selderij')

chimpanzee.why: 'Chimpanseen' is not a Dutch form. Van Dale: de chimpansee -> de chimpansees. The word entered Dutch via French chimpanze and patterns with the French -ee group (tournee->tournees, matinee->matinees), not with the native/Greek group that takes -een (zee->zeeen, idee->ideeen).

chips.why: 'Chipsen' is not a Dutch word - the script appended -en to a form that is already plural. The plural is 'chips'; per the file convention p equals s.

clementine.why: Van Dale: de clementine -> de clementines. A French-origin fruit name in -ine takes -s (cf. aubergine -> aubergines, nectarine -> nectarines); 'Clementinen' comes from the script's default -en rule.

coach.why: Van Dale: de coach -> de coaches. English loanword in -ch takes -es; 'Coachen' comes from the script's default -en rule (and collides with the Dutch verb 'coachen').

cocktail.why: Van Dale: de cocktail -> de cocktails. 'Cocktailen' is the script's default -en rule and reads as a verb.

columbine.why: Van Dale: de akelei -> de akeleien. The apostrophe-s plural applies only after an unstressed a/i/o/u/y; 'akelei' ends in the diphthong -ei and takes -en (cf. vallei -> valleien, kraai -> kraaien).

cook.why: Van Dale: de kok -> de koks. 'Kokken' is the script's consonant-doubling rule misfiring (and reads as the verb 'kokkelen'/dialect). Note key 'chef' already has the correct 'Chef-koks' - the file contradicts itself.

cooler.why: Van Dale: de box -> de boxen, so de koelbox -> de koelboxen. 'Koelboxxen' is the script's consonant-doubling rule applied to x, which Dutch never doubles.

croissant.why: Van Dale: de croissant -> de croissants. French loanword in -ant takes -s (cf. restaurant -> restaurants); 'Croissanten' is the script's default -en rule.

crossing-guard.why: Van Dale: de regelaar -> de regelaars, so de verkeersregelaar -> de verkeersregelaars. Deverbal agent nouns in -aar take -s (winnaar -> winnaars, luisteraar -> luisteraars); the -aren plural exists only for a few lexicalised exceptions (leraren, ambtenaren), which this is not.

crow.why: Van Dale: de kraai -> de kraaien. The apostrophe-s plural applies only after an unstressed a/i/o/u/y; 'kraai' ends in the diphthong -aai and takes -en (cf. haai -> haaien).

cruise-ship.why: Van Dale: het schip -> de schepen (irregular vowel change), so het cruiseschip -> de cruiseschepen. 'Cruiseschippen' is the script's consonant-doubling rule and is not a Dutch word.

cupcake.why: Van Dale: de cupcake -> de cupcakes. English loanword takes -s; 'Cupcaken' is the script's default -en rule and reads as a verb.

desk.why: the apostrophe-s plural is only for words ending in a single vowel letter a/i/o/u/y (auto's, foto's); -eau is a digraph spelling, so the plural is written without an apostrophe

detective.why: English loanword; takes -s. 'Detectiven' is a script-generated -en plural and is not Dutch

dragonfly.why: final-syllable stress (li-BEL) triggers consonant doubling; 'Libels' is the script's default -s and is not Dutch

eclair.why: French loanword; takes -s. 'Eclairen' is the script's -en default and is not Dutch

eggplant.why: nouns ending in an unstressed schwa -e take -s, not -n. 'Auberginen' is not Dutch

electric-drill.why: 'machine' ends in an unstressed schwa -e and takes -s. 'Boormachinen' is not Dutch

elf.why: this is the very -lf -> -lven script rule the brief names for 'Kalven': it fired here too. Standard Dutch is 'elfen'; 'elven' is fantasy-genre usage, not the dictionary plural

espresso-machine.why: unstressed schwa -e takes -s; 'Espressomachinen' is not Dutch

excavator.why: unstressed schwa -e takes -s; 'Graafmachinen' is not Dutch

forklift.why: English loanword 'truck' takes -s: de (vork)heftruck -> vorkheftrucks. 'Vorkheftrucken' is a blind -en rule applied to an English loan

french-fries.why: In Standard Dutch (NL) 'patat' (the dish) is a mass noun: 'een bakje patat', no plural. 'Patatten' exists only in southern/Flemish dialect where it means potatoes (aardappelen) - a different referent from the pictured fries

frisbee.why: de frisbee -> frisbees (English loan takes -s); 'Frisbeen' is not Dutch

garlic.why: Knoflook is a mass noun (stofnaam); no child-facing plural. 'Knofloken' is additionally a malformed vowel-shortening artefact of the script

gerbil.why: de gerbil -> gerbils (English loan takes -s). 'Gerbillen' is a blind -en rule with consonant doubling

gift.why: Words in -eau take plain -s: het cadeau -> de cadeaus (cf. bureaus, niveaus). The apostrophe rule applies only to a single final vowel letter a/i/o/u/y, which -eau is not
gift.src: Woordenlijst Nederlandse Taal (Groene Boekje) / Van Dale

glue.why: Lijm is a mass noun (stofnaam), like water/melk. 'Lijmen' is formally attested but only in the sorts-of-glue sense; for a classroom image of a glue bottle it is not a child-facing plural

grapefruit.why: de grapefruit -> grapefruits (English loan takes -s); 'Grapefruiten' is a blind -en rule

grill.why: de grill (appliance) -> grills (English loan takes -s). 'Grillen' is wrong twice over: it is the plural of the unrelated 'de gril' (whim) and identical to the verb 'grillen' - a real hazard for a text-to-speech site

hawk.why: de havik -> de haviken, with a SINGLE k: nouns in unstressed -ik do not double the consonant (monnik -> monniken, perzik -> perziken, leeuwerik -> leeuweriken). 'Havikken' is the script's blind consonant-doubling rule

hoodie.why: de hoodie -> hoodies (English loan takes -s); 'Hoodien' is not Dutch

hot-cocoa.why: chocolademelk is a mass noun exactly like melk (the brief's own example); 'chocolademelken' does not exist. p becomes s

hummingbird.why: stress is ko-LI-brie, so the final -ie is unstressed and takes -s: kolibries. The -en/-ien form only applies to stressed -ie (knie -> knieen, industrie -> industrieen)

jaguar.why: de jaguar -> jaguars. 'Jaguaren' is the script's -en rule; the loanword takes -s

jam.why: jam is a mass noun (stofnaam) exactly like the brief's water/melk/zout; 'Jammen' is the script's consonant-doubling artifact. A count plural only exists for varieties ('jams' = soorten jam), which is not child-directed and does not match a supermarket/breakfast picture. p becomes s. NB this is the opposite of bread -> broden, which does have a countable unit (a loaf); jam has none

janitor.why: de conciërge ends in a schwa -e and therefore takes -s: conciërges. 'Conciërgen' is the script's -en rule

jeep.why: de jeep -> jeeps. 'Jepen' applies Dutch vowel shortening to an English loanword and produces a non-word

jelly-beans.why: 'Jellybeansen' is impossible: it inflects an already-plural English loan a second time. The plural is jellybeans. NB this leaves s = p until the singular HOLD above is resolved

jumpsuit.why: de jumpsuit -> jumpsuits; English loanword takes -s. 'Jumpsuiten' is the script's -en rule

kayak.why: stress is KA-jak (first syllable), so no consonant doubling: de kajak -> kajaks. 'Kajakken' is not only the script's doubling artifact, it is also the infinitive of the verb kajakken, which a TTS voice would read as an action, not a plural

kettlebell.why: English loanword with first-syllable stress -> -s: kettlebells. 'Kettlebellen' is the script's -en rule (and reads as the verb 'bellen')

lawn-mower.why: instrument/agent nouns in unstressed -er take -s: de grasmaaier -> grasmaaiers. 'Grasmaaieren' is the script's -en rule

leek.why: de prei -> preien. 'Prei's' is orthographically impossible: the apostrophe before -s is only used after a single vowel letter (a/i/o/u/y), never after the digraph -ei

leggings.why: de legging -> leggings; this garment loan keeps the English -s plural. NB not every -ing loan does (training -> trainingen), which is exactly why this needs the word-by-word call rather than a rule

lemonade.why: limonade ends in an unstressed schwa -e (li-mo-NA-de) and therefore takes -s, like salade -> salades. 'Limonaden' is the script's -en rule. Unlike jam in this batch, limonade does have a natural child-audible count use (portions: 'twee limonades'), so NO_PLURAL would be wrong here

lemur.why: 'Lemurren' is impossible: doubling requires a stressed final syllable, and the stress is LE-mur. The established Dutch zoological plural is 'lemuren' (from Latin lemures)

life-preserver.why: de boei -> boeien. 'Reddingsboei's' is orthographically impossible: the apostrophe before -s is only used after a single vowel letter, never after -oei

light-switch.why: non-person nouns in -aar take -s: de schakelaar -> schakelaars. 'Lichtschakelaren' is the script's -en rule (the -aren plural belongs to person nouns like leraar -> leraren, not to instruments)

lightning.why: de bliksem is a mass/phenomenon noun; no child-directed plural (N1 confirmed). 'Bliksems' additionally reads as the interjection/intensifier 'bliksems', which a TTS voice would render as an exclamation. p becomes s

lily.why: stress is LE-lie, so the final -ie is unstressed and takes -s: lelies. 'Lelien' is a non-word either way - even the stressed pattern would give -ieen, never -ien

macaron.why: French loanword: de macaron -> de macarons; 'Macaronnen' comes from the script's consonant-doubling rule, which does not apply to this loan

magnifying-glass.why: het glas -> de glazen (vowel lengthening + s/z devoicing alternation); compound inherits it: vergrootglas -> vergrootglazen. 'Vergrootglassen' is a doubling artefact

manatee.why: de koe -> de koeien (irregular); the compound follows: zeekoe -> zeekoeien. 'Zeekoen' is a generated form that does not exist

mechanic.why: de monteur -> de monteurs. The -euren plural is limited to a small closed set of Latinate agent nouns (directeuren, redacteuren) and does not extend to monteur; cf. chauffeurs, masseurs, acteurs

medal.why: de medaille -> de medailles (French loanword ending in a schwa syllable takes -s); 'Medaillen' does not exist

medical-chart.why: two errors: het dossier -> de dossiers (not -en), and the attributive adjective must inflect in the plural. The script inflected only the last token

microphone.why: de microfoon -> de microfoons, like telefoon -> telefoons, grammofoon -> grammofoons. 'Microfonen' is not a Dutch form

microwave.why: de/het magnetron -> de magnetrons; 'Magnetronnen' is a consonant-doubling artefact and is not used for the appliance

milkshake.why: English loanword: de milkshake -> de milkshakes; 'Milkshaken' is a generated form and would read as a verb

monster-truck.why: English loanword: de monstertruck -> de monstertrucks; 'Monstertrucken' would read as a verb

morning-glory.why: 'Dagbloemen' is a different plant altogether (dagbloem = Commelina), not a plural of 'winde'. de winde -> de winden

nectarine.why: de nectarine -> de nectarines (loanword in schwa takes -s, cf. aubergines, machines); 'Nectarinen' does not exist

oatmeal.why: mass noun: de havermout has no child-relevant plural. 'Havermouten' is a generated form; p must become 'Havermout'. The N1 flag is correct here

oil.why: themes=[at_the_supermarket] -> cooking oil, a mass noun; p must become 'Olie'. 'Olien' is doubly wrong: it is a generated form, and even the real plural (types of oil) would be 'olien' with a trema -> 'oliën'

onion.why: de ui -> de uien. 'Ui's' misapplies the apostrophe-s rule, which is only for words ending in a single stressed vowel letter (a/i/o/u/y: ara's, taxi's); 'ui' ends in the digraph <ui>

orangutan.why: de orang-oetan -> de orang-oetans (Malay loanword takes -s); 'Orang-oetannen' is a consonant-doubling artefact

orchid.why: de orchidee -> de orchideeen requires the trema: 'orchideeen' is not a legal Dutch spelling. Stem in -ee + -en takes a diaeresis on the e (cf. zee -> zeeen -> zeeën)

ottoman.why: de poef (French loan 'pouf') -> de poefs. 'Poeven' applies the native f/v alternation (brief -> brieven), which does not extend to this loanword

padlock.why: Van Dale: het slot -> de sloten (open-syllable lengthening), so hangslot -> hangsloten. 'Hangslotten' is the script's blind consonant-doubling rule; slot does NOT double (contrast pot -> potten)

parrot.why: Van Dale: de papegaai -> de papegaaien. The apostrophe-s is only for words ending in a single long vowel (a/i/o/u/y): panda's, pony's. 'Papegaai' ends in the diphthong -aai and takes -en. 'Papegaai's' is not Dutch at all

pasta.why: mass noun (de pasta), theme=at_the_supermarket. 'Pasta's' only exists as 'types of pasta' — not the child-facing reading. p must become 'Pasta'. N1 flag correct here

peach.why: Van Dale: de perzik -> de perziken. Stress is PER-zik: the final syllable is UNSTRESSED, so no consonant doubling (cf. monnik->monniken, havik->haviken). 'Perzikken' is the script's blind doubling rule

pickup-truck.why: Van Dale: de pick-up -> de pick-ups. English loans take -s; 'Pick-uppen' is the script's doubling rule and is not Dutch

picnic.why: Van Dale: de picknick -> de picknicks (English loan takes -s). 'Picknicken' is not a plural at all — it is the INFINITIVE 'to picnic'. Read aloud to a child this is a verb where a noun is expected

porridge.why: mass noun (de pap), theme=breakfast. p must become 'Pap'. 'Pappen' is not a plural at all — it is the verb 'to poultice/paste' (script doubling rule). N1 flag correct here

potato-chips.why: 'Chipsen' is not Dutch — it is the script adding -en to an already-plural loan. The plural is 'chips', unchanged (p == s)

present.why: Van Dale: het cadeau -> de cadeaus. The apostrophe is only for a single final vowel; -eau takes a bare -s (cf. bureaus, niveaus). 'Cadeau's' is a spelling error

purse.why: Van Dale: de portemonnee -> portemonnees. Nouns ending in unstressed/-ee take -s; 'Portemonneen' is output of the script rule that blindly appends -n to -e words (same defect as Saladen, Naaimachinen, Punaisen)

push-pin.why: Van Dale: de punaise -> punaises. Noun ending in schwa takes -s; 'Punaisen' is the -e+n script rule again

rain.why: mass noun exactly like the brief's water/melk/zout. Van Dale does list 'regens' but only for meteorological/literary countings of rainfalls; with themes=nature,spring and a picture of rain shown to a 3-7 year old, no plural exists. metadata countable:true is the known-fallible hint (cf. bread)

rhino.why: Van Dale: de neushoorn -> neushoorns. 'hoorn' does not pluralise in -en (Van Dale: hoorn -> hoorns/horens); 'hoornen' is the ADJECTIVE (een hoornen bril), not a plural. 'Neushoornen' is a script artefact and is not a Dutch word

rhinoceros.why: identical defect to key 'rhino': de neushoorn -> neushoorns, not 'Neushoornen'

rubber-boot.why: SEVERE: de laars -> de LAARZEN (s->z voicing), never 'laarsen'. Proven internally inconsistent by this very batch, which has the correct 'Regenlaarzen' at key rain-boots. 'rubberen' stays uninflected (participle/material adjective in -en)

salad.why: Van Dale: de salade -> salades. 'Saladen' is the -e+n script rule (same defect as Portemonneen, Punaisen, Naaimachinen)

salt.why: the brief's own worked example, and it holds: themes=at_the_supermarket -> this is kitchen salt, a mass noun. 'Zouten' is the chemical/technical plural (classes of salts) and is flatly wrong for a supermarket picture shown to a 3-7 year old. metadata countable:true is the known-fallible hint

science.why: abstract/mass noun as used here. 'de wetenschappen' is a real Dutch plural (the academic disciplines, cf. natuurwetenschappen) - but with themes=activities and en Science/Science the referent is the school activity, for which no plural exists. N1 correctly flagged

screwdriver.why: SEVERE: de schroevendraaier -> schroevendraaiers. Agent nouns in -er take -s, never -en; 'Schroevendraaieren' is not a Dutch word at all. The same batch gets this right at vogelverschrikkers, deegrollers, papegaaiduikers and salamanders, which proves it is an isolated script artefact

scrubs.why: 'kleding' is a mass noun and has no plural in Dutch; 'Operatiekledingen' is not a word. p must become s (Operatiekleding). Note the en gloss being plural ('Scrubs') does not make the Dutch countable - Dutch expresses the pair/set with the mass noun

sewing-machine.why: Van Dale: de machine -> machines, so de naaimachine -> naaimachines. 'Naaimachinen' is the -e+n script rule again

shark.why: SEVERE and unambiguous: Van Dale de haai -> de HAAIEN. 'Haai's' is not Dutch under any rule - the apostrophe rule never applies to -aai (a digraph/trigraph, not a single-letter long vowel), and a Dutch TTS would read 'Haai's' as /haːis/. This is the worst form in the batch: a very common K-3 animal word

smoothie.why: de smoothie -> de smoothies. 'Smoothien' is not a Dutch word; it comes from the script appending -(e)n. English loans in -ie take -s

spinach.why: spinazie is a mass noun; 'Spinazien' is not a Dutch word (script artefact). p must become s = 'Spinazie'. The N1 flag is correct here

spray.why: de spray -> de sprays. The apostrophe rule applies only to a stressed single vowel LETTER at the end (auto's, taxi's, ski's); -ay is not that case. Compare essays, displays, jockeys

stapler.why: de machine -> de machines, so nietmachine -> nietmachines. 'Nietmachinen' is not a Dutch word; the script appended -n to a word already ending in -e

stork.why: de ooievaar -> de ooievaars. The -aren plural is restricted to a small set of agent nouns (leraar -> leraren); non-agentive bird names in -aar take -s, exactly like adelaar -> adelaars. 'Ooievaren' carries the script's mechanical -en fingerprint and is additionally read as a verb-like form

strawberry.why: de aardbei -> de aardbeien. The apostrophe rule was misapplied: it only applies after a stressed single vowel letter (taxi's, auto's); -ei is a digraph and takes plain -en

stretcher.why: de brancard -> de brancards. Unnaturalized French loans in -ard take -s (boulevard -> boulevards); 'Brancarden' is the script's mechanical -en

submarine.why: de onderzeeër -> de onderzeeërs. Nouns in -er/-eër take -s, never -en. 'Onderzeeëren' is not a Dutch word; the script appended -en

sundae.why: de coupe -> de coupes, so ijscoupe -> ijscoupes. 'IJscoupen' comes from the script appending -n to a word already ending in -e

sunscreen.why: de crème -> de crèmes, so zonnebrandcrème -> zonnebrandcrèmes (kinds/tubes; same calibration as brood -> broden, so NOT a mass-noun case). 'Zonnebrandcrèmen' is the script's -n on a word already ending in -e

swallow.why: Van Dale: de zwaluw -> zwaluwen. 'Zwaluwwen' is the script's consonant-doubling rule misfiring: w is never doubled after the digraph 'uw'.

sweater.why: Van Dale: de trui -> truien. 'Trui's' applies the apostrophe rule for words ending in a single vowel; 'ui' is a digraph, so the plural is -en.

t-rex.why: Dutch never doubles x (fax -> faxen, box -> boxen), so 'T-Rexxen' is impossible spelling. Plural is T-rexen.
t-rex.src: Woordenlijst Nederlandse Taal (spelling rule: x is not doubled)

tank.why: Van Dale: de tank -> tanks. 'Tanken' is not a plural at all, it is the verb 'to refuel' - a child would hear the wrong word entirely.

telephone.why: Van Dale: de telefoon -> telefoons (like microfoon -> microfoons, xylofoon -> xylofoons). 'Telefonen' is not current Dutch.

television.why: Van Dale: de televisie -> televisies. 'Televisien' is a machine-generated -en form that does not exist.

tennis-racket.why: Van Dale: het racket -> rackets. Stress is on the first syllable, so the consonant-doubling rule that produced 'racketten' does not apply.

thunderstorm.why: Weather phenomenon, not counted in child-facing Dutch ('het onweer'). Van Dale does record a rare plural 'onweren', so I do not call the current form a hard spelling error - but it is not a word to speak to a 3-7 year old; several thunderstorms are 'onweersbuien'. p = s per the file convention.

toothpaste.why: Mass noun (de tandpasta); 'Tandpasta's' would mean brands/kinds, not what the picture shows. p becomes s.

toucan.why: Van Dale: de toekan -> toekans. The loanword does not carry final-syllable stress, so the script's consonant-doubling rule ('Toekannen') does not apply.

trail.why: Van Dale: het pad -> de paden. 'Padden' is the plural of the ANIMAL 'de pad'; the script applied the toad's doubling rule to the footpath, so a child sees a trail and hears 'toads'.

trillium.why: 'blad' has a long a, so consonant doubling is impossible - 'Driebladden' cannot be a Dutch word. Compounds in -blad take -bladen (tafelblad -> tafelbladen, dekblad -> dekbladen); 'bladeren' is reserved for leaves on a tree.

tyrannosaurus-rex.why: Dutch never doubles x (fax -> faxen, box -> boxen), so 'Rexxen' is impossible spelling. Pure form correction of the same lemma; the alternative 'tyrannosaurussen' would change the lemma, so I did not use it.
tyrannosaurus-rex.src: Woordenlijst Nederlandse Taal (spelling rule: x is not doubled)

unicorn.why: Van Dale: de eenhoorn -> eenhoorns. 'Eenhoornen' is not a valid plural of hoorn (which is hoorns/horens); 'hoornen' only exists as an adjective ('een hoornen bril').

wallet.why: de portemonnee -> de portemonnees. 'Portemonneen' is a script artefact (bare -n added to a French loan ending in -ee); no such Dutch form exists

wand.why: de staf -> de staven (f/v alternation, like graf -> graven), so de toverstaf -> de toverstaven. 'Toverstaffen' is the script's consonant-doubling rule misfiring on a word that takes voicing instead

washing-machine.why: de machine -> de machines, so de wasmachine -> de wasmachines. 'Wasmachinen' is a script artefact (bare -n on a word ending in unstressed -e)

watch.why: het horloge -> de horloges. 'Horlogen' is a script artefact (bare -n on a word ending in unstressed -e)

water-lily.why: de lelie -> de lelies, so de waterlelie -> de waterlelies. 'Waterlelien' is a script artefact (bare -n on -ie)

whisk.why: de garde -> de gardes. 'Garden' is a script artefact (bare -n on unstressed -e) and is additionally a false friend with English 'garden' on a projected board

armadillo.why: het dier -> het gordeldier. Compounds with -dier as head are neuter; the script's default 'd' is wrong

badminton.why: het badminton. Dutch sport/game names are neuter (het tennis, het voetbal, het hockey); themes=sports + type verb-gerund + no English plural show the sport is depicted, not an object

baking.why: substantivized infinitives are always neuter: het bakken

baseball.why: het honkbal (the sport), like het voetbal/het basketbal. Caveat for the operator: if the picture in fact shows the BALL, the correct form is 'de honkbal' - the gender is the meaning distinction here; the metadata (no English plural, verb-gerund, themes sports/activities) points to the sport

basketball.why: het basketbal (the sport). Same caveat as honkbal: 'de basketbal' would be the ball itself; the metadata points to the sport

biking.why: substantivized infinitives are always neuter: het fietsen

blue.why: as a noun the colour is neuter: het blauw. 'd' is the script default (bug)

bowling.why: substantivised infinitives are always neuter: het bowlen. 'd' is the script default (bug)

boxing.why: substantivised infinitives are always neuter: het boksen. 'd' is the script default (bug)

brown.why: as a noun the colour is neuter: het bruin. 'd' is the script default (bug)

camp.why: het kamp (encampment, holiday camp) -> de kampen; theme travel_and_holiday fixes this reading. 'de kamp' is a different word (contest/enclosed field). 'd' is the script default (bug)

camping.why: the activity is the substantivised infinitive het kamperen (always neuter). Note: 'de camping' (campsite) is a different noun and is not what type=verb-gerund/en=Camping encodes here

chess.why: Substantivized infinitives are always neuter: het schaken (cf. het zwemmen). The script's fallthrough assigned 'd'.

chick.why: Van Dale: het kuiken -> de kuikens. Not a diminutive, so the script's -je rule missed it and it fell through to 'd'.

computer-keyboard.why: Van Dale: het bord -> het toetsenbord -> het computertoetsenbord (de computertoetsenborden). Compound gender comes from the head noun 'bord', which is neuter; -bord was not on the earlier suffix-bounded search list, so this survived as 'd'.

cruise-ship.why: Compound gender comes from the head noun: het schip -> het cruiseschip. The script's fallthrough gave 'd'.

dancing.why: Substantivized infinitives are always neuter: het dansen (cf. het zwemmen). 'd' would only be right for the unintended reading 'de dans -> de dansen'.

dogwood-tree.why: de kornoelje is a common-gender noun. The script's diminutive rule (endsWith('je')) misfired on the lexical ending -je of kornoelje; it is not a diminutive. 'Het kornoelje' is not Dutch

drink.why: a substantivized infinitive is always neuter in Dutch: het drinken. 'De drinken' is impossible under any reading
drink.src: Van Dale / general rule: substantivized infinitives are het-words

ear.why: het oor. Straight instance of the script's default-to-'d' bug; 'de oor' is not Dutch
ear.src: Van Dale: het oor - de oren

eat.why: substantivized infinitive is always neuter: het eten. Consistent with key 'food' (N6 collision), which already carries 'h' for the same word

fishing.why: substantivized infinitive is always neuter: het vissen. 'De vissen' would be the plural of the fish, i.e. exactly the wrong reading for this key
fishing.src: Van Dale / general rule: substantivized infinitives are het-words

foal.why: het veulen. Another instance of the default-to-'d' bug; 'de veulen' is not Dutch (compare het kalf, het veulen, het lam - young-animal nouns are largely neuter)
foal.src: Van Dale: het veulen - de veulens

football.why: Dutch sport names are neuter: het voetbal, het hockey, het rugby -> het American football. 'De American football' is not Dutch. (If the picture were to show the ball rather than the sport, the whole lemma would be wrong - but every metadata field says sport)

gingerbread-house.why: Head noun is 'het huis', so het peperkoekhuis. The script's default-to-'de' bug; a child would hear 'de peperkoekhuis'

golf.why: HOMONYM, gender IS the meaning: de golf = wave/gulf; het golf = the ball game. The 'sports' theme fixes the game reading, so it must be 'h'. Dutch sport names are neuter (het voetbal, het tennis, het hockey)

gray.why: Nominalised colour names are neuter: het grijs (cf. het groen, het rood). 'De grijs' is not Dutch; 'd' here is the script's default-to-de bug

green.why: Nominalised colour names are neuter: het groen. 'De groen' is not Dutch; 'd' is the script default

hiking.why: Nominalised infinitives are always neuter: het wandelen (cf. the brief's own 'het zwemmen'). 'De wandelen' is not Dutch; 'd' is the script default

hockey.why: Dutch sport names are neuter: het hockey (cf. het voetbal, het tennis, het golf). 'De hockey' is not Dutch; 'd' is the script default

ice-skating.why: substantivized infinitives are ALWAYS neuter in Dutch: het schaatsen, not de schaatsen. The 'd' is the script default described in the brief

jumping.why: substantivized infinitives are always neuter: het springen, not de springen

knitting.why: substantivized infinitives are always neuter: het breien, not de breien

magnifying-glass.why: het vergrootglas, like het glas. The generator's default 'd' is wrong; this compound was invisible to the earlier suffix-bounded sweep

post-office.why: het kantoor -> het postkantoor. This is exactly the genderNl bug: no suffix on the rule's list, so it fell through to the 'd' default. A child would hear 'de postkantoor'

pottery.why: substantivized verbs are always het: het pottenbakken. The file's own convention confirms it — the sibling activity key painting->'Schilderen' is already coded h. 'd' here is the genderNl default-fallthrough bug

read.why: substantivised infinitives are ALWAYS neuter in Dutch: HET lezen. The brief's own example 'het zwemmen' confirms the class. 'd' is the genderNl fall-through bug

reading.why: het lezen - substantivised infinitives are neuter without exception

rocking-horse.why: HET paard -> HET hobbelpaard. Van Dale: hobbelpaard (het; o; meervoud hobbelpaarden). This is the genderNl fall-through bug exactly as described: nothing in the word matches the het-suffix list, so it was defaulted to 'd'. A child would hear 'de hobbelpaard'

run.why: het rennen - substantivised infinitives are neuter (brief: het zwemmen)

running.why: het rennen - substantivised infinitives are neuter

scuba-diving.why: het duiken - substantivised infinitives are neuter (brief: het zwemmen)

sewing.why: het naaien - substantivised infinitives are neuter

singing.why: substantivized infinitives are always neuter in Dutch: HET zingen. The brief itself writes 'het zwemmen'. 'd' would produce *de zingen

sit.why: as a bare verb no article applies, but the only defensible value if it is ever rendered with one is neuter: HET zitten (substantivized infinitive). 'd' can only ever be wrong

skating.why: HET schaatsen (the activity). 'd' encodes the OTHER lemma (de schaatsen = the skates) and would make the entry say the wrong thing

skiing.why: het skiën (the activity). Contrast de ski -> de ski's (the object)

sledding.why: het sleeën (the activity). Homographic with 'de sleeën' = the sleds (plural of slee), which is exactly why 'd' is wrong here

sleep.why: only defensible value is neuter: HET slapen (substantivized infinitive)

snorkeling-mask.why: the head noun is 'masker', which is neuter: HET masker -> HET snorkelmasker. Current 'd' is a genderNl default (the word matches none of the script's suffixes), and would produce *de snorkelmasker

soccer.why: HOMONYM, and gender IS the meaning here, exactly the Kiefer trap: HET voetbal = the sport (this key: themes [activities, sports], en 'Soccer'), DE voetbal = the ball (key 'soccer-ball'). Current 'd' makes this entry say 'the ball' while the image/gloss is the sport. The N6 collision with soccer-ball is the tell

stand.why: only defensible value is neuter: HET staan (substantivized infinitive)

swimming.why: Nominalised infinitives are always neuter: het zwemmen. The generator's fallback returned 'd'.

table-tennis.why: Sport names are neuter in Dutch: het tafeltennis (cf. het tennis, het voetbal).

tape.why: Van Dale / Woordenlijst: het plakband (Standard Dutch, Netherlands). The generator's catch-all returned 'd'.

tape-measure.why: Head noun 'lint' is neuter (het lint, de linten), so het meetlint. The generator's catch-all returned 'd'.

tennis.why: Sport names are neuter: het tennis.

violet.why: safe regardless of how the singular resolves: substantivised colour names are neuter (het violet, cf. het rood) AND the flower is a diminutive (het viooltje). Both candidate lemmas are het-words, so 'd' is wrong either way

walk.why: substantivised infinitives are always neuter: het lopen. 'd' is the genderNl fall-through bug

watch.why: het horloge is neuter; 'd' is the genderNl fall-through bug

white.why: when a colour name is used as a noun it is neuter: het wit (cf. het rood, het blauw). 'd' is the genderNl fall-through bug and would generate the ungrammatical 'de wit'

writing.why: substantivised infinitives are always neuter: het schrijven. 'd' is the genderNl fall-through bug

yacht.why: homonym trap: themes [vehicles/travel] -> het jacht (the boat, neuter), whereas de jacht is HUNTING. The data currently encodes the hunt, not the pictured boat; 'd' would make a child hear 'de jacht'

yellow.why: when a colour name is used as a noun it is neuter: het geel (cf. het rood). 'd' is the genderNl fall-through bug and would generate the ungrammatical 'de geel'. NB the script's own code even special-cases 'geel' out of its ge- rule, which is why it fell through to 'd'
